package application

import (
	"context"

	"metaldocs/internal/platform/authn"
)

// A3.3 negative fixture (Rule 2): the CANONICAL accessor, called correctly,
// with its presence result thrown away.
//
// This is the failure mode that makes Rule 1 alone insufficient. Rule 1 removes
// the fail-open accessor from the runtime; this file shows the fail-open shape
// coming straight back through the fail-closed one, because the difference
// between "absence is a decision" and "absence is an empty string" is one
// underscore wide. `actorID, _ :=` compiles, reads like migrated code, and
// yields exactly the "" that Rule 1 was written to eliminate.
//
// The second declaration pins the error-returning sibling: RequireUserID exists
// so a consumer below the delivery layer can refuse WITHOUT importing net/http,
// and discarding its error defeats that just as completely.
//
// Both are matched by import PATH, so aliasing internal/platform/authn does not
// exempt them either.
//
// See scripts/testdata/guard-fixtures/README.md.
func settleInvoice(ctx context.Context) string {
	actorID, _ := authn.UserIDFromContext(ctx)
	return actorID
}

func voidInvoice(ctx context.Context) string {
	actorID, _ := authn.RequireUserID(ctx)
	return actorID
}
